section_summary: This section consists chiefly of prewar licensing and representation agreements concerning Japanese manufacture and sale of magnets, gears, propellers, steel tubes, engines, and industrial equipment. It also includes correspondence about Dorr and Oliver equipment, a list of Dorr’s Japanese patents, and the opening of a 1946 despatch enclosing an Allied directive on zaibatsu family property.

subfiles.title: German–Sumitomo agreement, concluding clauses and signature
subfiles.about: The surviving clauses address arbitration, governing law, taxes, and administration of the agreement.
subfiles.summary: The agreement assigns contract administration within the German group to Siemens & Halske and records signatures at Berlin and Osaka.

subfiles.title: Cyclo gear licence agreement
subfiles.about: Cyclo licenses Sumitomo to make and sell patented cycloidal gears in Japan and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: The agreement sets territorial sales limits, machinery and design transfers, engineer training, secrecy obligations, payments, and royalties. It provides for patent improvements, inspections, penalties for unauthorized sales, and a term through 1951.

subfiles.title: Draft magnet steel patent and licensing agreement
subfiles.to: Deutsche Edelstahlwerke, Siemens & Halske, and Siemens-Schuckertwerke
subfiles.about: The parties propose reciprocal licensing and territorial rules for patented permanent magnet steels.
subfiles.summary: The draft replaces a preliminary agreement of 17 March 1934. It allocates European and Japanese rights in nickel–titanium and cobalt–nickel–titanium magnet steels, including sublicensing and sales to third markets. It sets reciprocal royalties, reporting, patent maintenance, sharing of technical improvements, and arbitration.

subfiles.title: VDM adjustable propeller licence agreement
subfiles.to: Sumitomo Kinzoku Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha, through Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha
subfiles.about: VDM grants Sumitomo exclusive manufacturing and sales rights for its adjustable aircraft propeller in Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The contract describes propeller components and provides for drawings, production methods, technical assistance, training, patent use, and territorial exclusivity. It requires a lump sum of £36,000, protects confidential material, and sets a ten-year term. The signature pages record execution in Berlin and contemplated acknowledgment in Osaka.

subfiles.title: Seamless steel tube process licence agreement
subfiles.from: Maschinenfabrik Meer A.G., Dr. Fritz Singer, and Tubus A.G.
subfiles.about: The agreement licenses a crank-press process for seamless steel tubes in Japan and other Asian territories.
subfiles.summary: The licensors grant exclusive process rights, provide technical knowledge and improvements, and specify royalties through 1940. Further clauses govern machinery manufacture, patent enforcement and fees, German law, and a twelve-year contract term ending in 1947.

subfiles.title: Summary of contract for manufacturing Lentz steam engines
subfiles.about: Mitsubishi describes its licence from Willy Salge & Co. to manufacture Lentz steam engines.
subfiles.summary: The summary lists manufacturing and sales rights, patents, a $20,000 purchase price, and five engines produced. Mitsubishi argues that cancellation would end production and waste its technical investment.

subfiles.title: Dorr–Sanki representative agreement and Schedule A
subfiles.about: Dorr appoints a Japanese representative to arrange manufacture and sale of specified Dorr equipment.
subfiles.summary: The agreement covers Japan and Manchukuo and permits manufacture through Toyo Babcock. It defines equipment and industry exclusions, technical support, drawings, patents, commissions, pricing, reporting, confidentiality, termination, and arbitration. Schedule A lists the covered machinery.

subfiles.title: Dorr–Sanki gross-profit distribution letter
subfiles.about: Dorr advises Sanki that its share of gross profit on new Dorr orders will rise to 40 percent.
subfiles.summary: The letter discusses the sales threshold and estimates 1939 Dorr business, including a Manchurian order.

subfiles.title: Sanki representation and pricing instructions
subfiles.about: Dorr provides Sanki with equipment books and instructions for estimating prices and dividing gross profit.
subfiles.summary: The letter explains how to use specifications, weights, drawings, and Toyo Babcock cost data; the second page bears a conflicting 1941 date.

subfiles.title: Dorr Japanese patents and applications
subfiles.about: The list identifies Dorr patents and applications in Japan with file numbers, inventions, and expiry dates.
subfiles.summary: Entries cover clarifiers, thickeners, flocculators, pumps, classifiers, screens, and related processes.

subfiles.title: Dorr–Oliver agreement with equipment and royalty schedules
subfiles.about: Oliver authorizes Dorr to arrange Japanese manufacture and sale of specified Oliver equipment through Sanki.
subfiles.summary: The agreement covers Japan and Manchukuo, sets equipment exclusions, and governs drawings, technical assistance, compensation, payments, reporting, and arbitration. Schedule A lists covered filters and related equipment; Schedule B lists inventor royalties. The signature page is dated 23 May 1937.

subfiles.title: Dorr letter authorizing Sanki to handle Oliver equipment
subfiles.from: D. S. McAfee, The Dorr Company
subfiles.about: Dorr invites Sanki to manufacture and market Oliver equipment under the new Dorr–Oliver agreement.
subfiles.summary: The letter explains territorial and product exclusions, allocation of royalties and gross profit, and use of Toyo Babcock for manufacture. It also addresses drawings, pricing, earlier Oliver business, and a correction to the Dorr–Sanki representative agreement.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 758 on transfer of zaibatsu family properties
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards SCAPIN 1363 concerning transfer of designated zaibatsu family assets.
subfiles.summary: The cover despatch encloses the Allied memorandum directing an expanded role for the Holding Company Liquidation Commission.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1363: Transfer of Zaibatsu Family Properties
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The memorandum directs Japan to empower the Holding Company Liquidation Commission to receive and manage designated family property.
subfiles.summary: The page cites earlier SCAP directives and orders expanded commission authority within five days; its text continues beyond this section.
